memos.risk:
Refuse. The coin is down 80% from its 30-minute high and 65% over 30 minutes, and the data shows heavy selling pressure (sell-to-buy ratio ~1.04, last-15-minute net flow of +1.46 SOL on 77 SOL of buying, nearly all of it churn). Recovery from a drawdown this deep is rare, and the launch-bot presence and unresolved curve data (bundle share, completer share, top3 share all null) mean we can't rule out a factory or wash pattern. Graduation delay is also unknown, and the name and symbol are null, so there's no metadata to sanity-check.

Pool depth of ~50 SOL is thin enough that a $20 ticket plus a 1.4-5.1% round trip would be unrecoverable against any stop move. Even if we ignored the trend, the base rates say skip.

If the desk wants a reconsideration path, the only thing that would change my view is a resolved curve (bundle and top3 shares known and not concentrated) plus evidence of net positive flow sustained over multiple windows, not one 15-minute snapshot.
memos.scout:
The strongest case for buying here is thin, and the brief itself undercuts most of it. Real demand would show up as sustained net inflow, but the last 15 minutes show net flow of +1.46 SOL on 77 SOL of buying, with 171 sellers against 172 buyers, so the book is essentially flat and sellers are keeping pace. The coin is down 80% from its 30-minute high and 65% over 30 minutes, which reads as a completed dump rather than a base forming. Early activity was heavy (241 buyers, 127 SOL in the first two minutes) but the sell-to-buy ratio of about 1.04 and the launch bot present point to the early buyers already exiting. Top-5 buyer concentration is moderate at 17%, which is a minor point in its favor, and the pool depth of 50 SOL is enough to exit a $20 ticket without catastrophic slippage.

Against a 1.4-5.1% round-trip cost and a 30-second execution lag, there is no evidence in the brief that demand will persist for the next 30-60 minutes. No honest case for buying now. Skip.
memos.skeptic:
Most likely loss: a slow bleed from insider distribution plus fee drag. The coin is already down 80% from its 30-minute high (drawdown 0.8005) and -65% over 30 minutes, so the dip has been running hard, not bottoming. In the last 15 minutes, sellers (171) nearly equal buyers (172), and sell SOL (75.59) almost matches buy SOL (77.05), netting only +1.46 SOL on roughly $18.7k of volume. That is dead, churning flow, not accumulation.

The launch was heavily bot-driven: a launch bot is present, and in the first two minutes sell-to-buy was 1.04, meaning early buyers were already exiting as fast as they came in. Graduation timing and curve data are null, so we cannot confirm operator backing, bundling, or whether the creator still holds supply. Name and symbol are null, so there is no metadata to lean on either way.

With a 50.6 SOL pool and a 1.4-5.1% round-trip cost, even a modest bounce would likely be eaten by fees and impact, while a further leg down from unresolved holder concentration is the realistic outcome. Skip.
